<p class="section-kicker">Course overview</p>
<h2>Built for research teams who need clean accelerometer data.</h2>
<p>Accelerometry turns continuous movement signals into information about activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep. This course follows the practical decisions that make that transformation credible: device setup, file organization, processing, quality control, cleaning, and documentation.</p>
<p>The course is intended for research assistants, students, analysts, and investigators who work with free-living accelerometer data. The examples use ActiGraph, GGIR in R, and Stata, but the principles are broader than any one device or software package.</p>
:::

::: {.section-wrap}
<p class="section-kicker">Before you start</p>
<h2>Choose the depth that fits your role.</h2>

::: {.workflow-grid .compact}
<div class="workflow-step"><span>A</span><strong>Concept route</strong><p>Read the lessons, use the video summaries or transcripts, and complete the self-checks. Allow about 3–4 hours. A web browser is sufficient.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>B</span><strong>Hands-on route</strong><p>Also complete each mini-activity and produce the module deliverables. Allow about 6–9 hours, excluding software installation and full-dataset processing.</p></div>
:::

::: {.review-note}
<strong>Hands-on prerequisites:</strong> Bring an approved or fictional study protocol and a safe practice dataset with no direct identifiers. Modules 2–3 require access to a compatible ActiGraph device and ActiLife for the demonstrated workflow. Modules 4–6 use R, RStudio, and GGIR. Module 7 uses Stata. ActiLife and Stata access may depend on your laboratory or institution's licensing. Record the exact device, firmware, and software versions used in your own project.
:::
:::

::: {.workflow-section #workflow}
::: {.section-wrap}
<p class="section-kicker">Workflow</p>
<h2>From device deployment to analysis-ready evidence.</h2>

::: {.workflow-grid}
<div class="workflow-step"><span>01</span><strong>Collect</strong><p>Initialize devices, define placement and wear protocol, and support participant compliance.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>02</span><strong>Download</strong><p>Retrieve raw recordings and document return status, dates, and operator decisions.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>03</span><strong>Organize</strong><p>Use reproducible folders, IDs, file naming, conversion logs, and transparent storage.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>04</span><strong>Process</strong><p>Run GGIR or another approved workflow to calibrate, detect non-wear, and summarize movement.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>05</span><strong>Inspect</strong><p>Review reports, missingness, calibration, clipping, valid days, and unusual movement patterns.</p></div>
<div class="workflow-step"><span>06</span><strong>Deliver</strong><p>Clean, standardize, derive outcomes, prepare Stata datasets, and report analytical decisions.</p></div>
:::
:::
:::

<section class="faq-section" id="faq" aria-labelledby="faq-heading">
<div class="section-wrap">
<p class="section-kicker">Course help</p>
<h2 id="faq-heading">Frequently asked questions</h2>
<p class="faq-intro">Start with the practical questions, then review the method and file-format questions.</p>

<h3>Getting started</h3>
<div class="faq-grid">
<details class="faq-item" open>
<summary>Who is this course for?</summary>
<p>It is designed for research assistants, students, analysts, and investigators who need a reproducible workflow for planning accelerometer studies, processing raw files, checking quality, and preparing analysis-ready datasets.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How long does the course take?</summary>
<p>Allow about 3–4 hours for the concept route or 6–9 hours for the hands-on route. Full-dataset processing, software installation, and protocol approval take additional time. Each module card shows a planning estimate.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Which devices and software does the course use?</summary>
<p>The examples use ActiGraph devices, ActiLife, GGIR in R, and Stata. You can complete the concept route in a browser. Hands-on work requires appropriate software and a safe practice dataset; access to ActiLife and Stata may depend on your laboratory or institution's licensing.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Do I need previous experience with R, GGIR, or Stata?</summary>
<p>No prior experience is required for the concept route. For the hands-on route, you should be comfortable finding files, editing paths, running a script, reading software messages, and protecting participant data. Basic familiarity with R and Stata is helpful in Modules 4–7.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How can I use the videos accessibly?</summary>
<p>Each video is followed by a quick summary, a full transcript, and a downloadable caption track. The summary is for rapid review; it is not a substitute for the transcript or captions. Software controls and visual-only details are described in the accompanying text where they affect the task.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>How do I know that I completed a module?</summary>
<p>Complete the self-check and compare your reasoning with the feedback. On the hands-on route, also save the module's stated deliverable—for example, a protocol decision, download log, GGIR configuration, QC log, or analysis script.</p>
</details>
</div>

<h3>Methods and files</h3>
<div class="faq-grid">
<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What does an accelerometer measure directly?</summary>
<p>It records acceleration over time, usually along three axes. Behaviors such as activity intensity, sedentary time, posture, and sleep are estimates derived from the raw signal using a documented algorithm, wear location, and protocol.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Does GGIR require conversion from <code>.gt3x</code> to <code>.csv</code>?</summary>
<p>No. GGIR can read <code>.gt3x</code> files directly. Convert to CSV only when a downstream script, another software package, data-sharing requirement, or audit workflow specifically needs it.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What is the difference between <code>.gt3x</code> and <code>.agd</code> files?</summary>
<p>A <code>.gt3x</code> file contains raw ActiGraph acceleration data. The demonstrated workflow also creates a 10-second <code>.agd</code>, a count-based epoch summary that may be useful for ActiLife review or legacy workflows. Follow the approved protocol if it specifies another epoch length.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What counts as a valid participant record?</summary>
<p>The course example uses at least 4 valid days, at least 10 hours of awake wear per valid day, and at least 1 weekend day. These are example rules and must be approved for the study population, device, placement, and protocol.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>Are the course thresholds and cleaning rules universal?</summary>
<p>No. Device settings, valid-day rules, intensity thresholds, wear criteria, and variable-specific cleaning rules are study-specific examples. Confirm every rule against the approved protocol, the exact software version, and the relevant output dictionary before applying it.</p>
</details>

<details class="faq-item">
<summary>What should the final analysis package contain?</summary>
<p>Include a dated <code>.dta</code> file, data dictionary, cleaning log, exclusion table, Stata do-file, and a README that identifies the source GGIR run and processing batches.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
</section>

::: {.section-wrap .decision-panel}
<div>
<p class="section-kicker">Protocol standard</p>
<h2>Every parameter needs a study reason.</h2>
</div>
<p>Device configuration, valid-day rules, wear-time criteria, thresholds, and processing arguments must be selected for the study population, device, wear location, and protocol. This course teaches the decision process; it does not prescribe one universal parameter set.</p>
